sentences.zh: 涼武昭王

translations.literal: Prince Wuzhao of Liang
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wuzhao of Liang

sentences.zh: 武昭王諱暠，字玄盛，小字長生，隴西成紀人，姓李氏，漢前將軍廣之十六世孫也。

translations.literal: The Prince Wuzhao's taboo name was Gao, style name Xuansheng, childhood name Changsheng, a man of Chengji in Longxi, surname Li, sixteenth-generation descendant of Han's former general Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wuzhao of Liang was Li Gao, courtesy Xuansheng, childhood name Changsheng, from Chengji in Longxi of the Li clan—the sixteenth generation down from the Han general Li Guang.

sentences.zh: 廣曾祖仲翔，漢初為將軍，討叛羌於素昌，素昌即狄道也，眾寡不敵，死之。

translations.literal: Guang's great-great-grandfather Zhongxiang was a general at the beginning of the Han, campaigned against rebel Qiang at Suchang—Suchang is Didao—and, outnumbered, died there.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guang's ancestor Zhongxiang served as a Han general against rebel Qiang at Suchang—that is, Didao—and died when his men were overwhelmed.

sentences.zh: 仲翔子伯考奔喪，因葬于狄道之東川，遂家焉，世為西州右姓。

translations.literal: Zhongxiang's son Bokao came for the mourning and therefore was buried east of the river at Didao; thereupon the family settled there and for generations were a great clan of the western provinces.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bokao came east to bury him below Didao, and the Li line put down roots there as one of the great houses of the northwest.

sentences.zh: 高祖雍，曾祖柔，仕晉並歷位郡守。

translations.literal: His high ancestor Yong and great-great-grandfather Rou both served the Jin and rose in turn to prefect.
translations.idiomatic: His remote ancestors Yong and Rou both served the Jin and rose to prefectural rank.

sentences.zh: 祖弇，仕張軌為武衛將軍、安世亭侯。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yan served Zhang Gui as General Who Guards the Marches and village marquis of Anshi.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yan was General Who Guards the Marches under Zhang Gui and village marquis of Anshi.

sentences.zh: 父昶，幼有令名，早卒，遺腹生玄盛。

translations.literal: His father Chang had a fine reputation in youth but died early; Xuansheng was born posthumously.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chang was famed in youth but died young; Xuansheng was a posthumous child.

sentences.zh: 少而好學，性沈敏寬和，美器度，通涉經史，尤善文義。

translations.literal: In youth he loved learning; his nature was deep, keen, generous, and mild; he had fine bearing and capacity; he read broadly in the classics and histories and was especially skilled in literary meaning.
translations.idiomatic: He loved books from boyhood—grave, quick, and even-tempered, with an imposing presence—and he read widely, excelling above all at letters and argument.

sentences.zh: 及長，頗習武藝，誦孫吳兵法。

translations.literal: When grown he studied military arts rather thoroughly and recited Sun and Wu's Art of War.
translations.idiomatic: As a man he took up the military arts and committed Sunzi and Wuzi to memory.

sentences.zh: 嘗與呂光太史令郭黁及其同母弟宋繇同宿，黁起謂繇曰：「君當位極人臣，李君有國土之分，家有騧草馬生白額駒，此其時也。」

translations.literal: He once lodged overnight with Lu Guang's grand astrologer Guo Nen and Nen's younger uterine brother Song Yao; Nen rose and said to Yao: "You will reach the summit of ministerial rank; Lord Li has a portion of a state; when a piebald mare of your house foals a white-browed colt, that will be the hour."
translations.idiomatic: Once he spent the night with Guo Nen, grand astrologer under Lu Guang, and Nen's half-brother Song Yao. Nen told Yao, "You will rise to the highest offices; this Li is fated for a realm of his own—when your dun mare drops a white-faced colt, the time has come."

sentences.zh: 呂光末，京兆段業自稱涼州牧，以敦煌太守趙郡孟敏為沙州刺史，署玄盛效穀令。

translations.literal: At the end of Lu Guang, Duan Ye of Jingzhao styled himself shepherd of Liangzhou; as prefect of Dunhuang he appointed Meng Min of Zhao commandery shepherd of Sha province and assigned Xuansheng magistrate of Xiaogu.
translations.idiomatic: Near Lu Guang's fall, Duan Ye of Jingzhao declared himself governor of Liang and named Meng Min of Zhao prefect of Dunhuang and Sha province, with Li Xuansheng as magistrate of Xiaogu.

sentences.zh: 敏尋卒，敦煌護軍馮翊郭謙、沙州治中敦煌索仙等以玄盛溫毅有惠政，推為甯朔將軍、敦煌太守。

translations.literal: Min soon died; Dunhuang protector Guo Qian of Pingyi, Sha province administrator Suo Xian of Dunhuang, and others, because Xuansheng was mild, resolute, and had benevolent government, recommended him as General Who Pacifies the Shakes and prefect of Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: When Meng Min died soon after, Dunhuang protector Guo Qian and administrator Suo Xian, finding Li Xuansheng gentle, firm, and a just magistrate, raised him to General Who Pacifies the Shakes and prefect of Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 玄盛初難之，會宋繇仕於業，告歸敦煌，言于玄盛曰：「兄忘郭黁之言邪？

translations.literal: Xuansheng at first demurred; it happened that Song Yao was serving Ye and, on leave returning to Dunhuang, said to Xuansheng: "Has elder brother forgotten Guo Nen's words?
translations.idiomatic: Li Xuansheng hesitated until Song Yao, home on leave from Duan Ye's court, said, "Brother, have you forgotten what Guo Nen foretold?

sentences.zh: 白額駒今已生矣。

translations.literal: The white-browed colt has now been born.
translations.idiomatic: The white-faced colt is already in your stable.

sentences.zh: 」玄盛乃從之。

translations.literal: Xuansheng thereupon followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xuansheng then accepted.

sentences.zh: 尋進號冠軍，稱籓於業。

translations.literal: Soon he advanced his title to General Who Crowns the Army and declared himself Ye's vassal.
translations.idiomatic: He soon took the title General Who Crowns the Army and acknowledged Duan Ye as his suzerain.

sentences.zh: 業以玄盛為安西將軍、敦煌太守，領護西胡校尉。

translations.literal: Ye appointed Xuansheng General Who Pacifies the West and prefect of Dunhuang, concurrently colonel who protects the western Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Ye named him General Who Pacifies the West and prefect of Dunhuang, with the added office of colonel of the western Hu.

sentences.zh: 及業僭稱涼王，其右衛將軍索嗣構玄盛於業，乃以嗣為敦煌太守，率騎五百而西，未至二十里，移玄盛使迫己。

translations.literal: When Ye usurped the title king of Liang, his guard general Suo Si slandered Xuansheng to Ye; Ye therefore appointed Suo Si prefect of Dunhuang, led five hundred horsemen westward, and, still twenty li short, sent Xuansheng a message ordering him to yield to himself.
translations.idiomatic: When Duan Ye took the title King of Liang, his guard general Suo Si poisoned the ear of the throne against Li Xuansheng; Ye named Suo Si prefect of Dunhuang and sent him west with five hundred horse, halting twenty li out to demand that Li Xuansheng step aside.

sentences.zh: 玄盛驚疑，將出迎之，效穀令經邈及宋繇止之曰：「呂氏政衰，段業暗弱，正是英豪有為之日，將軍處一國成資，奈何束手於人！

translations.literal: Xuansheng was startled and doubtful and was about to go out to welcome him; Xiaogu magistrate Jing Miao and Song Yao stopped him, saying: "The Lu house's government declines; Duan Ye is dim and weak—this is exactly the day for a hero to act; the general holds the completed resources of a state—how can you bind your hands for another!
translations.idiomatic: Li Xuansheng wavered and meant to ride out to meet Suo Si, but Jing Miao of Xiaogu and Song Yao barred him: "Lu's power fades and Duan Ye is a weakling—this is the hour for a strong hand. You already hold a ready state—why surrender meekly?

sentences.zh: 索嗣自以本邦，謂人情附己，不虞將軍卒能距之，可一戰而擒矣。

translations.literal: Suo Si, supposing himself native to this land, thought hearts would attach to him; he does not expect that the general can finally resist him—with one battle he can be captured.
translations.idiomatic: Suo Si fancies himself a local favorite and assumes the people will flock to him; he never thinks you can defy him—one stroke will take him.

sentences.zh: 」宋繇亦曰：「大丈夫已為世所推，今日便授首於嗣，豈不為天下笑乎！

translations.literal: Song Yao also said: "A great man already pushed by the age—today to surrender your head to Si—would it not be laughed at by the realm!
translations.idiomatic: Song Yao added, "You are already the choice of the hour—to lay your neck before Suo Si would make the empire laugh.

sentences.zh: 大兄英姿挺傑，有雄霸之風，張王之業不足繼也。

translations.literal: Elder brother's heroic bearing stands out; you have the wind of hegemony; the enterprises of common kings are not worth continuing."
translations.idiomatic: Your bearing is kingly; you carry the air of a hegemon—the petty thrones of ordinary lords are beneath you."

sentences.zh: 」玄盛曰：「吾少無風雲之志，因官至此，不圖此郡士人忽爾見推。

translations.literal: Xuansheng said: "In youth I had no ambition of wind and clouds; because of office I reached here; I did not expect the gentlemen of this commandery suddenly to push me.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xuansheng answered, "I never dreamed of greatness; office brought me here. I never thought your gentry would thrust this burden on me.

sentences.zh: 向言出迎者，未知士大夫之意故也。

translations.literal: What I said about going out to welcome was because I did not yet know the intent of the gentlemen of the capital."
translations.idiomatic: I spoke of riding out only because I had not yet taken your measure."

sentences.zh: 」因遣繇覘嗣。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent Yao to spy on Si.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Song Yao to scout Suo Si.

sentences.zh: 繇見嗣，啖以甘言，還謂玄盛曰：「嗣志驕兵弱，易擒耳。

translations.literal: Yao saw Si, fed him sweet words, returned, and said to Xuansheng: "Si's will is arrogant and his troops weak—he is easy to capture."
translations.idiomatic: Song Yao paid Suo Si honeyed compliments, returned, and reported, "He is cocky and his force is thin—easy prey."

sentences.zh: 」於是遣其二子士業、讓與邈、繇及以司馬尹建興等逆戰，破之，嗣奔還張掖。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent his two sons Shiye and Rang with Miao, Yao, and staff supervisor Yin Jianxing and others to meet him in battle, defeated him, and Si fled back to Zhangye.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent his sons Shiye and Rang with Jing Miao, Song Yao, Yin Jianxing, and others to meet Suo Si in the field, broke him, and drove him back to Zhangye.

sentences.zh: 玄盛素與嗣善，結為刎頸交，反為所構，故深恨之，乃罪狀嗣于段業。

translations.literal: Xuansheng had always been on good terms with Si, sworn friends who would die for each other, yet Si slandered him in turn; therefore he deeply hated him and laid charges against Si to Duan Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Though he and Suo Si had been sworn friends, Suo Si had betrayed him with slander; Li Xuansheng nursed a bitter grudge and memorialized every crime to Duan Ye.

sentences.zh: 業將且渠男又惡嗣，至是，因勸除之。

translations.literal: Ye's general Juqu Nan also hated Si; at this point he therefore urged removing him.
translations.idiomatic: Juqu Nan, another of Ye's generals, loathed Suo Si and now urged his execution.

sentences.zh: 業乃殺嗣，遣使謝玄盛，分敦煌之涼興、烏澤、晉昌之宜禾三縣為涼興郡，進玄盛持節、都督涼興已西諸軍事、鎮西將軍，領護西夷校尉。

translations.literal: Ye thereupon killed Si, sent envoys to apologize to Xuansheng, divided Dunhuang's Liangxing, Wuze, and Jinchang's Yihe—three counties—to form Liangxing commandery, and advanced Xuansheng to credential holder, area commander of all military affairs west of Liangxing, General Who Garrisons the West, concurrently colonel who protects the western Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Ye executed Suo Si, apologized to Li Xuansheng, carved three counties from Dunhuang and Jinchang into a new Liangxing commandery, and promoted him to baton-bearing area commander west of Liangxing, General Who Garrisons the West, and colonel of the western Yi.

sentences.zh: 時有赤氣起于玄盛後園，龍跡見於小城。

translations.literal: At that time red vapor rose from Xuansheng's rear garden, and dragon tracks appeared in the small city.
translations.idiomatic: A red mist rose from his rear garden and dragon prints showed on a lesser rampart.

sentences.zh: ，晉昌太守唐瑤移檄六郡，推玄盛為大都督、大將軍、涼公、領秦涼二州牧、護羌校尉。

translations.literal: Then prefect of Jinchang Tang Yao circulated a proclamation through six commanderies and recommended Xuansheng as grand commander-in-chief, grand general, duke of Liang, concurrently shepherd of Qin and Liang two provinces, and colonel who protects the Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: Then Tang Yao of Jinchang sent a call across six commanderies, raising Li Xuansheng to grand commander, grand general, Duke of Liang, governor of Qin and Liang, and colonel of the Qiang.

sentences.zh: 玄盛乃赦其境內，建年為庚子，追尊祖弇曰涼景公，父昶涼簡公。

translations.literal: Xuansheng thereupon amnestied his territory, established the year as Gengzi, posthumously honored his grandfather Yan as duke Jing of Liang and his father Chang as duke Jian of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed an amnesty, adopted the Gengzi era name, and posthumously titled his grandfather Yan Prince Jing of Liang and his father Chang Prince Jian of Liang.

sentences.zh: 以唐瑤為征東將軍，郭謙為軍諮祭酒，索仙為左長史，張邈為右長史，尹建興為左司馬，張體順為右司馬，張條為牧府左長史，令狐溢為右長史，張林為太府主簿，宋繇、張謖為從事中郎，繇加折沖將軍，謖加揚武將軍，索承明為牧府右司馬，令狐遷為武衛將軍、晉興太守，氾德瑜為甯遠將軍、西郡太守，張靖為折沖將軍、河湟太守，索訓為威遠將軍，西平太守，趙開為騂馬護軍、大夏太守，索慈為廣武太守，陰亮為西安太守，令狐赫為武威太守，索術為武興太守，以招懷東夏。

translations.literal: He appointed Tang Yao General Who Punishes the East, Guo Qian libationer of military counsel, Suo Xian left chief clerk, Zhang Miao right chief clerk, Yin Jianxing left marshal, Zhang Tishun right marshal, Zhang Tiao left chief clerk of the shepherd's office, Linghu Yi right chief clerk, Zhang Lin senior recorder of the grand treasury, Song Yao and Zhang Su as retainers—Yao added General Who Smashes the Charge, Su added General Who Rouses Might—Suo Chengming right marshal of the shepherd's office, Linghu Qian General Who Guards the Marches and prefect of Jinxing, Fan Deyu General Who Pacifies the Distance and prefect of Xijun, Zhang Jing General Who Smashes the Charge and prefect of Hehuang, Suo Xun General Who Rouses the Distance and prefect of Xiping, Zhao Kai escort of piebald horses and prefect of Daxia, Suo Ci General Who Displays Might, Yin Liang prefect of Xi'an, Linghu He prefect of Wuwei, Suo Shu prefect of Wuxing, in order to summon and comfort the eastern summer.
translations.idiomatic: He filled his government from Tang Yao eastward to the marches—Guo Qian as war counsel, Suo Xian and Zhang Miao as left and right chiefs, Yin Jianxing and Zhang Tishun as marshals, a sweep of frontier prefects from Wuwei to Hehuang, and a host of other posts—to draw the east under his influence.

sentences.zh: 又遣宋繇東伐涼興，並擊玉門已西諸城，皆下之，遂屯玉門、陽關，廣田積穀，為東伐之資。

translations.literal: He also sent Song Yao east to campaign against Liangxing and jointly strike the cities west of Yumen; all fell; he then garrisoned Yumen and Yang Pass, broadened fields and stored grain, as resources for eastern campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Song Yao east against Liangxing and the towns beyond Yumen, took them all, and planted garrisons at Yumen and Yang Pass, farming and granarying for a future march east.

sentences.zh: 初，呂光之稱王也，遣使市六璽玉于于闐，至是，玉至敦煌，納之郡府。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Lu Guang styled himself king, he had sent envoys to buy the six seals' jade in Khotan; at this time the jade reached Dunhuang and was stored in the commandery treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Guang, when he claimed kingship, had sent to Khotan for the jade of the six imperial seals; that stone now reached Dunhuang and was locked in the treasury.

sentences.zh: 仍于南門外臨水起堂，名曰靖恭之堂，以議朝政，閱武事。

translations.literal: He still south of the outer gate beside the water raised a hall named the Hall of Serene Reverence, to deliberate court government and review military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: South of the south gate, overhanging the water, he built the Hall of Serene Reverence for state councils and martial reviews.

sentences.zh: 圖贊自古聖帝明王、忠臣孝子、烈士貞女，玄盛親為序頌，以明鑒戒之義，當時文武群僚亦皆圖焉。

translations.literal: He had painted eulogies of sage emperors and enlightened kings, loyal ministers and filial sons, fierce martyrs and chaste women, from antiquity; Xuansheng personally composed prefaces and hymns to clarify the meaning of mirror and warning; at that time civil and military officials likewise all had portraits done.
translations.idiomatic: Its walls bore portraits and hymns of ancient paragons—sage kings, loyal ministers, filial sons, and steadfast women—with prefaces in his own brush to teach mirror and warning; his high officers too sat for their likenesses.

sentences.zh: 有白雀翔於靖恭堂，玄盛觀之大悅。

translations.literal: There were white sparrows circling the Serene Reverence Hall; Xuansheng watched them and was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: White sparrows wheeled above the hall; he watched them with deep pleasure.

sentences.zh: 又立泮宮，增高門學生五百人。

translations.literal: He also founded a school of the pond and increased the high-gate students to five hundred.
translations.idiomatic: He founded a state academy and raised the student body to five hundred.

sentences.zh: 起嘉納堂於後園，以圖贊所志。

translations.literal: He raised the Hall of Joyful Reception in the rear garden to paint and praise what he aspired to.
translations.idiomatic: In the rear garden he built the Hall of Joyful Reception to picture and hymn his aims.

sentences.zh: ，玄盛改元為建初，遣舍人黃始、梁興間行奉表詣闕曰：

translations.literal: Then Xuansheng changed the era name to Jianchu and sent retainers Huang Shi and Liang Xing by secret route to present a memorial at the palace gate, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He then adopted the Jianchu era and sent Huang Shi and Liang Xing by covert paths to the capital with a memorial that began:

sentences.zh: 昔漢運將終，三國鼎峙，鈞天之曆，數鐘皇晉。

translations.literal: In old days the Han fortune was ending; the three kingdoms stood like a tripod; the calendar of the Pole Star turned to the august Jin.
translations.idiomatic: When the Han waned, the three kingdoms balanced like a tripod until Heaven's calendar swung to the great Jin.

sentences.zh: 高祖闡鴻基，景文弘帝業，嗣武受終，要荒率服，六合同風，宇宙齊貫。

translations.literal: The high ancestor opened the vast foundation; Jing and Wen enlarged the imperial enterprise; the heir received the mandate's end; the farthest wastes submitted; the six directions shared one wind; the universe was threaded as one.
translations.idiomatic: The dynastic founder laid the base; Wen and Jing widened the throne; the successor took the mandate; the farthest wastes bowed; the realm breathed as one.

sentences.zh: 而惠皇失馭，權臣亂紀，懷湣屯邅，蒙塵於外，懸象上分，九眼下裂，眷言顧之，普天同憾。

translations.literal: But Emperor Hui lost the reins; powerful ministers threw the norms into chaos; Emperors Huai and Min wandered in distress, dust-stained abroad; portents split above; the nine provinces cracked below; looking back with care, all under Heaven shared the same regret.
translations.idiomatic: Then Emperor Hui lost the reins, great ministers wrecked the law, and Emperors Huai and Min wandered in dust without court; heaven showed fissures and the nine provinces gaped; every loyal heart grieved as one.

sentences.zh: 伏惟中宗元皇帝基天紹命，遷幸江表，荊揚蒙弘覆之矜，五都為荒榛之藪。

translations.literal: Humbly I reflect: Emperor Zhongzong, the Yuan emperor, took Heaven's foundation and continued the mandate, moved favor to south of the Yangzi; Jing and Yang received his sheltering pity; the five capitals became thickets of wasteland.
translations.idiomatic: Your ancestor Emperor Yuan took up Heaven's thread south of the river, while Jing and Yang sheltered under him and the five capitals turned to wilderness.

sentences.zh: 故太尉、西平武公軌當元康之初，屬擾攘之際，受命典方，出撫此州，威略所振，聲蓋海內。

translations.literal: The former grand commandant, Duke Wu of Xiping, Gui, at the beginning of Yuankang, amid turmoil and upheaval, received mandate to control the region, went out to pacify this province; where his majesty and strategy shook, his fame covered the inner seas.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gui, late grand commandant and Duke Wu of Xiping, in the first Yuankang years took charge of this march amid turmoil and brought such awe that his name filled the realm.

sentences.zh: 明盛繼統，不損前志，長旌所指，仍辟三秦，義立兵強，拓境萬里。

translations.literal: Ming sheng inherited the succession, not diminishing the earlier resolve; wherever the long banners pointed, he still opened Sanqin; righteousness established and arms strong, he widened borders ten thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: His brilliant heir carried the work forward: wherever banners flew, Sanqin opened again, and righteous arms stretched the frontier ten thousand li.

sentences.zh: 文桓嗣位，奕葉載德，囊括關西，化被崐裔，遐邇款籓，世修職貢。

translations.literal: Wen Huan succeeded the throne; generation after generation bore virtue; he embraced Guanzhong; transformation reached the offspring of Kun; far and near paid court as vassals; generation after generation repaired tribute duty.
translations.idiomatic: Wen and Huan kept the line in virtue, held all lands west of the pass, and spread civilization to the western marches until every neighbor sent tribute generation after generation.

sentences.zh: 晉德之遠揚，翳此州是賴。

translations.literal: The Jin virtue's far display—this province alone supported it.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin's glory abroad rested on this province alone.

sentences.zh: 大都督、大將軍天錫以英挺之姿，承七世之業，志匡時難，克隆先勳，而中年降災，兵寇侵境，皇威遐邈，同獎弗及，以一方之師抗七州之眾，兵孤力屈，社稷以喪。

translations.literal: The grand commander-in-chief, grand general Tiansi, with heroic bearing, inherited seven generations' enterprise, his will to rescue the age's crisis and enlarge the ancestors' merit, yet in mid-life met calamity; soldiers and bandits invaded the borders; imperial majesty was far distant; joint aid could not arrive; with one region's army he resisted seven provinces' hosts; the army isolated and strength exhausted—the altars therefore perished.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tianxi, last grand commander of Former Liang, bore seven generations of duty and meant to save the times, yet midlife disaster struck: invaders ringed him while the distant throne could send no aid. One province faced seven and fell; the state died with him.

sentences.zh: 臣聞歷數相推，歸余於終，帝王之興，必有閏位。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that the succession of calendars pushes the remainder to the end; the rise of emperors and kings must have an intercalary position.
translations.idiomatic: I have read that when one dynasty nears its term, another must rise between the cracks of fate.

sentences.zh: 是以共工亂象于黃農之間，秦項篡竊于周漢之際，皆機不轉踵，覆束成凶。

translations.literal: Therefore Gonggong disturbed the portents between Huangdi and Shennong; Qin and Xiang usurped between Zhou and Han—all turned on a heel and toppled into disaster.
translations.idiomatic: So Gonggong troubled the age between Huangdi and Shennong, and Qin and Xiang seized power between Zhou and Han—each fell as fast as he rose.

sentences.zh: 自戎狄陵華，已涉百齡，五胡僭襲，期運將杪，四海顒顒，懸心象魏。

translations.literal: Since the Rong and Di overran the Huaxia, already a hundred years have passed; the five Hu usurped in turn; the allotted fortune nears its end; the four seas crane their necks; hearts hang on the capital towers.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians have trampled the heartland for a century; the five Hu have seized thrones in turn; the mandate thins; every eye turns toward your capital.

sentences.zh: 故師次東關，趙魏莫不企踵；

translations.literal: Therefore when the army halted at Dongguan, Zhao and Wei all stood on tiptoe;
translations.idiomatic: When your host camped at Dongguan, Zhao and Wei watched on tiptoe;

sentences.zh: 淮南大捷，三方欣然引領。

translations.literal: the great victory at Huainan—three sides joyfully stretched their necks.
translations.idiomatic: and the great victory at Huainan set three corners of the realm straining to see.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下道協少康，德侔光武，繼天統位，志清函夏。

translations.literal: Humbly I reflect: Your Majesty's way matches Shao Kang; your virtue equals Guang Wu; you continue Heaven's line and stand in the succession; your will is to clear the letter summer.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty matches Shao Kang in purpose and Guangwu in virtue; you have taken Heaven's line and mean to cleanse the north.

sentences.zh: 至如此州，世篤忠義，臣之群僚以臣高祖東莞太守雍、曾祖北地太守柔荷寵前朝，參忝時務，伯祖龍驤將軍、廣晉太守、長寧侯卓，亡祖武衛將軍、天水太守、安世亭侯弇毗佐涼州，著功秦隴，殊寵之隆，勒於天府，妄臣無庸，輒依竇融故事，迫臣以義，上臣大都督、大將軍、涼公、領秦涼二州牧、護羌校尉。

translations.literal: As for this province, generation after generation has been steeped in loyalty and righteousness; your subject's host of officials, because your subject's high ancestor Yong, prefect of Dongguan, and great-great-grandfather Rou, prefect of Beidi, received favor from the former court and joined the affairs of the time, and because your subject's grand-uncle Zhuo, dragon-rising general, prefect of Guangjin, marquis of Changning, and deceased grandfather Yan, general who guards the marches, prefect of Tianshui, village marquis of Anshi, aided and attached Liangzhou and achieved merit in Qin and Long—the extraordinary favor was inscribed in Heaven's treasury—your worthless subject, without merit, rashly following Dou Rong's precedent, compelled by righteousness, elevated your subject to grand commander-in-chief, grand general, duke of Liang, concurrently shepherd of Qin and Liang two provinces, colonel who protects the Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: This land has been loyal age after age. My officers cite my ancestors' service under the Jin and the Former Liang—granduncle Zhuo, grandfather Yan, and the rest who built Liangzhou—and the honors recorded in the celestial archive; though I am unworthy, they pressed me, as Dou Rong was once pressed, to take grand command, the dukedom of Liang, and the governorship of Qin and Liang with the Qiang colonelcy.

sentences.zh: 臣以為荊楚替貢。

translations.literal: Your subject considers that Jing and Chu have ceased tribute.
translations.idiomatic: I note that tribute from Jing and Chu has failed.

sentences.zh: 齊桓興召陵之師，諸侯不恭，晉文起城濮之役，用能勳光踐土，業隆一匡，九域賴其弘猷，《春為》恕其專命。

translations.literal: When Duke Huan of Qi raised the army at Shaoling, the lords were disrespectful; when Duke Wen of Jin launched the campaign at Chengpu, thereby he was able to make merit shine at Ji'tu and enterprise rise in the single rectification; the nine regions relied on his great plan; the Spring and Autumn Annals forgave his acting on his own authority.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Huan of Qi marched when lords withheld duty; Duke Wen of Jin struck Chengpu and so lit his name at Ji'tu and raised the work of uniting the realm—the nine provinces rode on his design, and the Spring and Autumn Annals excused his acting without orders.

sentences.zh: 功冠當時，美垂幹祀。

translations.literal: Merit crowned the age; beauty hangs for a thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: Their merit crowned their age and still shines a thousand years later.

sentences.zh: 況今帝居未復，諸夏昏墊，大禹所經，奄為戎墟，五嶽神山，狄汙其三，九州名都，夷穢其七，辛有所言，於茲而驗。

translations.literal: Moreover now the imperial residence is not restored; the central states are drowned in darkness; what the Great Yu surveyed is swallowed as Rong wastes; of the five march-divinities three are fouled by Di; of the nine provinces' famed cities seven are befouled by Yi—what Xin You spoke of is verified here.
translations.idiomatic: Today the capital lies in ruins, the heartland drowned; lands Yu once traced are barbarian wastes; three of the five sacred peaks are defiled and seven of the nine great cities lie in alien hands—Xin You's warning has come true.

sentences.zh: 微臣所以叩心絕氣，忘寢與食，雕肝焦慮，不遑寧息者也。

translations.literal: This is why your petty subject knocks his heart and cuts off breath, forgets sleep and food, carves his liver in anxious thought, and has no leisure to rest.
translations.idiomatic: That is why I tear my breast, forsake sleep and food, and cannot rest a single night.

sentences.zh: 江涼雖遼，義誠密邇，風雲苟通，實如脣齒。

translations.literal: Although Jiang and Liang are distant, in righteousness they are truly close as lips and teeth; if wind and clouds once connect, it is truly like lips and teeth.
translations.idiomatic: River and Liang are far apart, yet in duty we are lip to tooth; should wind and clouds once align, we would stand as close as mouth to mouth.

sentences.zh: 臣雖名未結於天臺，量未著於海內，然憑賴累祖寵光餘烈，義不細辭，以稽大務，輒順群議，亡身即事。

translations.literal: Although your subject's name has not been tied to the celestial terrace and his measure is not marked within the seas, yet relying on accumulated ancestors' favor and the brilliance of their remaining glory, in righteousness he cannot lightly decline, to delay the great task; he has rashly followed the host of counsels, lost his person to take up the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Though I am unknown at court and untried in the realm, I lean on my forebears' honors and cannot, in good faith, shrink from the great charge; I have bowed to my officers' will and staked my life on the work.

sentences.zh: 轅弱任重，懼忝威命。

translations.literal: The cart is weak yet the burden heavy; I fear disgracing awesome command.
translations.idiomatic: My team is weak for so heavy a load; I dread shaming your mandate.

sentences.zh: 昔在春秋，諸侯宗周，國皆稱元，以布時令。

translations.literal: In old days in the Spring and Autumn period the lords took Zhou as ancestor; states all called their first month "yuan" to publish the seasons' orders.
translations.idiomatic: In the Spring and Autumn era the lords honored Zhou and each styled his first month "yuan" to proclaim the calendar.

sentences.zh: 今天台邈遠，正朔未加，發號旋令，無以紀數。

translations.literal: Now the celestial terrace is far distant; correct beginning has not been applied; issuing commands and rotating orders, there is no means to count the years.
translations.idiomatic: The court is far and your correct calendar has not reached us; we have no regnal count to follow.

sentences.zh: 輒年冠建初，以崇國憲。

translations.literal: Rashly I prefix the year with Jianchu to honor the state's statutes.
translations.idiomatic: I therefore prefix my dates with Jianchu to honor your law.

sentences.zh: 冀杖寵靈，全制一方，使義誠著於所天，玄風扇於九壤，殉命灰身，隕越慷慨。

translations.literal: I hope, leaning on favor and numinous power, wholly to control one region, cause righteousness and sincerity to shine toward Heaven, let mysterious wind fan the nine soils, and offer life in ashes and body in ruin, leaping beyond in generous devotion.
translations.idiomatic: May I, leaning on your favor, hold this corner loyally, spread your breeze through the nine provinces, and spend my life and body in your service.

sentences.zh: 玄盛謂群僚曰：「昔河右分崩，群豪競起，吾以寡德為眾賢所推，何嘗不忘寢與食，思濟黎庶。

translations.literal: Xuansheng said to the host of officials: "In old days the west of the river split apart and many heroes rose together; I, with scant virtue, was pushed by the worthies of the age—how could I forget sleep and food, thinking to save the black-haired people?
translations.idiomatic: Li Xuansheng told his council that when the Hexi broke apart and heroes contended, they had chosen him, though he lacked virtue, and that he had not slept for thinking of the people.

sentences.zh: 故前遣母弟繇董率雲騎，東殄不庭，軍之所至，莫不賓下。

translations.literal: Therefore earlier I sent my uterine brother Yao to lead the cloud cavalry east to destroy the disobedient; wherever the army went, none failed to submit.
translations.idiomatic: I sent my brother Yao east at the head of our best horse to punish rebels, and every town his banners touched submitted.

sentences.zh: 今惟蒙遜鴟跱一城。

translations.literal: Now only Mengxun perches like an owl on one city.
translations.idiomatic: Only Juqu Mengxun still squats like an owl on a single hold.

sentences.zh: 自張掖已東，晉之遺黎雖為戎虜所制，至於向義思風，過於殷人之望西伯。

translations.literal: East of Zhangye, the Jin's surviving common people, although controlled by Rong and barbarian captors, as for turning toward righteousness and longing for civilizing wind, exceed the Yin people's hope for the lord of the west.
translations.idiomatic: East of Zhangye the Jin survivors, though under barbarian rule, long for your grace more keenly than the Shang once longed for the lord of the west.

sentences.zh: 大業須定，不可安寢，吾將遷都酒泉，漸逼寇穴，諸君以為何如？

translations.literal: The great enterprise must be settled; one cannot rest in peace; I will move the capital to Jiuquan, gradually pressing the bandits' lair—what do the gentlemen think?"
translations.idiomatic: The great work must be finished; we cannot sleep at ease. I will shift the seat to Jiuquan and close on the enemy—what say you?"

sentences.zh: 」張邈贊成其議，玄盛大悅曰：「二人同心，其利斷金。

translations.literal: Zhang Miao praised his plan; Xuansheng was greatly pleased and said: "When two men share one heart, their sharpness can cut metal.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Miao backed the plan. Li Xuansheng exclaimed, "Two minds as one can cut through metal.

sentences.zh: 張長史與孤同矣，夫復何疑！

translations.literal: The chief clerk Zhang shares isolation with me—what further doubt is there!"
translations.idiomatic: The chief clerk stands with me—what doubt can remain?"

sentences.zh: 」乃以張體順為甯遠將軍、建康太守，鎮樂涫，征宋繇為右將軍，領敦煌護軍，與其子敦煌太守讓鎮敦煌，遂遷居於酒泉。

translations.literal: Thereupon he appointed Zhang Tishun General Who Pacifies the Distance and prefect of Jiankang, garrisoned Lègu; he summoned Song Yao as General of the Right, concurrently Dunhuang protector, with his son, Dunhuang prefect Rang, to garrison Dunhuang; then he moved residence to Jiuquan.
translations.idiomatic: He named Zhang Tishun General Who Pacifies the Distance and prefect of Jiankang to hold Lègu, recalled Song Yao as General of the Right and Dunhuang protector with his son Rang as Dunhuang prefect, and moved his own seat to Jiuquan.

sentences.zh: 手令誡其諸子曰：

translations.literal: By handwritten order he admonished his various sons, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He wrote his sons a private admonition that began:

sentences.zh: 初，玄盛之西也，留女敬愛養于外祖尹文。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Xuansheng went west, he left his daughter Jing'ai to be raised by her maternal grandfather Yin Wen.
translations.idiomatic: When he first marched west he left his daughter Jing'ai in the care of her grandfather Yin Wen.

sentences.zh: 文既東遷，玄盛從姑梁褒之母養之。

translations.literal: After Wen had moved east, Xuansheng's aunt on his father's side, the mother of Liang Bao, raised her.
translations.idiomatic: When Yin Wen went east, his aunt, Liang Bao's mother, took the girl in.

sentences.zh: 其後禿髮傉檀假道於北山。

translations.literal: Afterward Tufa Rutan borrowed a road through the northern hills.
translations.idiomatic: Later Tufa Rutan asked passage through the northern hills.

sentences.zh: 鮮卑遣褒送敬愛於酒泉，並通和好。

translations.literal: The Xianbei sent Bao to escort Jing'ai to Jiuquan and open good relations.
translations.idiomatic: The Xianbei sent Liang Bao to escort Jing'ai to Jiuquan and sue for peace.

sentences.zh: 玄盛遣使報聘，贈以方物。

translations.literal: Xuansheng sent envoys in return visit and presented local products.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xuansheng answered with envoys and gifts of his own.

sentences.zh: 玄盛親率騎二萬，略地至於建東，鄯善前部王遣使貢其方物，且渠蒙遜來侵，至於建康，掠三千餘戶而歸。

translations.literal: Xuansheng personally led twenty thousand horsemen to raid territory as far as Jiandong; the forward king of Shanshan sent envoys to offer local products; Juqu Mengxun came to invade as far as Jiankang, plundered more than three thousand households, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He led twenty thousand horse to raid east as far as Jiandong; the king of Shanshan sent tribute, but Juqu Mengxun struck Jiankang and dragged off three thousand households.

sentences.zh: 玄盛大怒，率騎追之，及于彌安，大敗之，盡收所掠之戶。

translations.literal: Xuansheng was greatly angry, led horsemen in pursuit, caught him at Mi'an, greatly defeated him, and fully recovered the plundered households.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xuansheng, furious, chased him to Mi'an, broke his army, and recovered every captive household.

sentences.zh: 初，苻堅建元之末，徙江漢之人萬餘戶于郭煌，中州之人有田疇不辟者，亦徙七千餘戶。

translations.literal: Earlier, at the end of Fu Jian's Jianyuan, he moved more than ten thousand households of the Jiang and Han people to Dunhuang; of central plain people who had fields not opened, he also moved more than seven thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Fu Jian's Jianyuan era he had resettled over ten thousand Jiang-Han families at Dunhuang and seven thousand more idle farmers from the central plain.

sentences.zh: 郭黁之寇武威，武威、張掖已東人西奔敦煌、晉昌者數千戶。

translations.literal: When Guo Nen raided Wuwei, several thousand households of people east of Wuwei and Zhangye fled west to Dunhuang and Jinchang.
translations.idiomatic: When Guo Nen struck Wuwei, thousands of families east of Wuwei and Zhangye fled west into Dunhuang and Jinchang.

sentences.zh: 及玄盛東遷。

translations.literal: When Xuansheng moved east.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Xuansheng shifted his seat eastward,

sentences.zh: 皆徙之於酒泉，分南人五千戶置會稽郡，中州人五千戶置廣夏郡，余萬三千戶分置武威、武興、張掖三郡，築城于敦煌南子亭，以威南虜，又以前表未報，復遣沙門法泉間行奉表，曰：

translations.literal: he moved them all to Jiuquan, divided five thousand southern households to establish Kuaiji commandery, five thousand central-plain households to establish Guangxia commandery, the remaining thirteen thousand households divided among Wuwei, Wuxing, and Zhangye three commanderies, built a city at Ziting south of Dunhuang to overawe the southern Lu, and because the earlier memorial had received no reply, again sent the monk Faquan by secret route to present a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: he resettled them at Jiuquan—five thousand southerners in a new Kuaiji command, five thousand northerners in Guangxia, the rest across Wuwei, Wuxing, and Zhangye—and walled Ziting south of Dunhuang to overawe the southern tribes. With no answer to his first memorial, he sent the monk Faquan again by hidden ways with a letter that read:

sentences.zh: 江山悠隔，朝宗無階，延首雲極，翹企遐方。

translations.literal: Rivers and mountains stretch far apart; there is no step to court; stretching the neck to the clouds' limit, I crane toward the distant quarter.
translations.idiomatic: Mountains and rivers divide us from your court; I can only crane my neck toward the sky and long for the capital.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下應期踐位，景福自天，臣去乙巳歲順從群議，假統方城，時遣舍人黃始奉表通誠，遙途險曠，未知達不？

translations.literal: Humbly I reflect: Your Majesty has answered the period and mounted the throne; bright blessing comes from Heaven; your subject, in the yisi year past, followed the host of counsels, provisionally commanded the square wall, then sent retainer Huang Shi with a memorial to declare sincerity; the road was distant and perilous—I do not know whether it arrived?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has taken the throne as Heaven ordains. In the past yisi year I bowed to my officers, took provisional command, and sent Huang Shi with a letter of loyalty along roads so long and rough that I still do not know if it reached you.

sentences.zh: 吳涼懸邈，蜂蠆充衢，方珍貢使，無由展禦，謹副寫前章，或希簡達。

translations.literal: Wu and Liang hang far apart; wasps and scorpions fill the roads; envoys of tribute and rare goods have no way to display their offerings; I respectfully append a fair copy of the earlier chapter, perhaps hoping for simple transmission.
translations.idiomatic: Wu and Liang are sundered; bandits choke the roads; no tribute train can get through. I enclose a fresh copy of my earlier memorial in hope it may win through.

sentences.zh: 臣以其歲進師酒泉，戒戎廣平，庶攘茨穢，而黠虜恣睢，未率威教，憑守巢穴，阻臣前路。

translations.literal: Your subject in that year advanced troops to Jiuquan, warned the troops at Guangping, hoped to sweep away the foul growth, yet the cunning Lu acted wantonly, did not follow awesome instruction, relied on guarding nest and den, and blocked your subject's forward road.
translations.idiomatic: That year I marched on Jiuquan and warned my host at Guangping, meaning to scour the land, but a cunning foe defied your command, clung to his den, and barred my road.

sentences.zh: 竊以諸事草創，倉帑未盈，故息兵按甲，務農養士。

translations.literal: Your petty subject considered that all affairs were grass beginnings and the granaries not yet full; therefore he rested troops and sheathed armor, devoted effort to farming and nurturing scholars.
translations.idiomatic: I judged the state still new and the bins thin, so I stood the army down and turned to plowing and schooling.

sentences.zh: 時移節邁，荏苒三年，撫劍歎憤，以日成歲。

translations.literal: As seasons shifted and nodes passed, three years flowed away; stroking the sword, sighing in resentment, the days became years.
translations.idiomatic: Three years slid by while I fingered my sword and nursed my anger day by day.

sentences.zh: 今資儲已足，器械已充，西招城郭之兵，北引丁零之眾，冀憑國威席捲河隴，揚旌秦川，承望詔旨，盡節竭誠，隕越為效。

translations.literal: Now stores are sufficient and weapons are filled; west I summon the wall cities' troops, north I draw the Dingling hosts; I hope, leaning on the state's majesty, to roll up He and Long, raise banners in Qin rivers, await your edict's intent, exhaust loyalty to the utmost, and leap beyond in devoted effect.
translations.idiomatic: Stores are full and arms ready; I can call garrisons from the west and Dingling riders from the north. If I may lean on your majesty, I mean to sweep He and Long and plant your banners in the Qin valleys—awaiting only your word to spend my life in your service.

sentences.zh: 又臣州界回遠，勍寇未除，當順鎮副為行留部分，輒假臣世子士業監前鋒諸軍事、撫軍將軍、護羌校尉，督攝前軍，為臣先驅。

translations.literal: Moreover your subject's province's borders wind far; fierce bandits are not yet removed; he ought to follow the deputy commander for mobile and stationary disposition; rashly he appoints his heir Shiye to supervise forward armies' military affairs, General Who Comforts the Army, colonel who protects the Qiang, to command and seize the forward army and go as your subject's vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: My march is vast and foes remain; I must split command between field and garrison. I therefore name my heir Shiye to lead the vanguard as supervisor of forward forces, General Who Comforts the Army, and colonel of the Qiang, riding before me.

sentences.zh: 又敦煌郡大眾殷，制禦西域，管轄萬里，為軍國之本，輒以次子讓為甯朔將軍、西夷校尉、敦煌太守，統攝昆裔，輯甯殊方。

translations.literal: Moreover Dunhuang commandery's population is great and prosperous; it controls the western regions and governs ten thousand li; it is root of army and state; rashly he appoints his second son Rang as General Who Pacifies the Shakes, colonel of the western Yi, Dunhuang prefect, to gather and govern Kun's descendants and pacify the different quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Dunhuang is thickly peopled, rules the Western Regions for ten thousand li, and is the root of army and state; I name my second son Rang General Who Pacifies the Shakes, colonel of the western Yi, and Dunhuang prefect to bind the western marches and quiet distant lands.

sentences.zh: 自余諸子，皆在戎間，率先士伍，臣總督大綱，畢在輸力，臨機制命，動靖續聞。

translations.literal: As for the remaining sons, all are among the troops, leading ahead of soldiers and officers; your subject holds the great outline in overall supervision, all bent on delivering strength; facing circumstance he issues commands; movement and stillness will be reported in succession.
translations.idiomatic: My other sons serve in the ranks ahead of the men while I hold the grand plan—every move will be reported as it comes.

sentences.zh: 玄盛既遷酒泉，乃敦勸稼穡。

translations.literal: After Xuansheng had moved to Jiuquan, he earnestly urged farming.
translations.idiomatic: Once settled at Jiuquan, Li Xuansheng threw his energy into agriculture.

sentences.zh: 郡僚以年穀頻登，百姓樂業，請勒銘酒泉，玄盛許之。

translations.literal: Commandery officials, because year after year the grain harvest mounted and the common people were content in their occupations, asked to inscribe a stele at Jiuquan; Xuansheng permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: His officers, seeing crop after crop succeed and the people thrive, asked leave to carve a monument at Jiuquan, and he agreed.

sentences.zh: 於是使儒林祭酒劉彥明為文，刻石頌德。

translations.literal: Thereupon he had forest-of-literature libationer Liu Yanming compose the text and carve stone praising his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: He had Liu Yanming, libationer of the academy, draft the inscription and set it in stone to hymn his rule.

sentences.zh: 既而蒙遜每年侵寇不止，玄盛志在以德撫其境內，但與通和立盟，弗之校也。

translations.literal: Soon Mengxun every year invaded and raided without cease; Xuansheng's will was to soothe his territory within with virtue; he only communicated peace and set a treaty with him and did not contend with him.
translations.idiomatic: Juqu Mengxun raided year after year, yet Li Xuansheng meant to rule within by virtue: he kept a treaty and would not answer blow for blow.

sentences.zh: 是時白狼、白兔、白雀、白雉、白鳩皆棲其園囿，其群下以為白祥金精所誕，皆應時邕而至，又有神光、甘露、連理、嘉禾眾瑞，請史官記其事，玄盛從之。

translations.literal: At this time white wolves, white hares, white sparrows, white pheasants, and white doves all roosted in his parks and preserves; his subordinates held that white auspices and the essence of metal had given birth to them, all arriving in season with harmonious sound; moreover there were divine light, sweet dew, linked branches, and fine grain—many auspices—and they asked the historiographer to record the affairs; Xuansheng followed them.
translations.idiomatic: White wolves, hares, sparrows, pheasants, and doves nested in his parks; his courtiers called it metal-phase auspice and asked the chronicler to record a shower of omens—sweet dew, twin trunks, bumper grain—and he consented.

sentences.zh: 尋而蒙遜背盟來侵，玄盛遣世子士業要擊敗之，獲其將且渠百年。

translations.literal: Soon Mengxun betrayed the treaty and came to invade; Xuansheng sent the heir Shiye to intercept and defeat him and captured his general Juqu Bainian.
translations.idiomatic: When Mengxun broke the pact, Li Xuansheng sent his heir Shiye to ambush him, broke his army, and took the general Juqu Bainian.

sentences.zh: 玄盛上巳日宴於曲水，命群僚賦詩。

translations.literal: On the shangsi day Xuansheng feasted at the winding canal and ordered the host of officials to compose poems.
translations.idiomatic: On the spring purification day he feasted by the winding stream and set his officers to verse.

sentences.zh: 而親為之序。

translations.literal: And personally for them composed a preface.
translations.idiomatic: He added a preface in his own brush.

sentences.zh: 於是寫諸葛亮訓誡以勖諸子曰：「吾負荷艱難，寧濟之勳未建，雖外總良能，憑股肱之力，而戎務孔殷，坐而待旦。

translations.literal: Thereupon he copied Zhuge Liang's admonitions to urge his various sons, saying: "I bear a heavy burden amid hardship; the merit of bringing peace is not yet established; although without I marshal able men and rely on the strength of arms and legs, yet military affairs are very pressing—I sit and await dawn.
translations.idiomatic: He copied Zhuge Liang's family admonitions for his sons: "I carry a heavy load in hard times; peace is not yet won. Though able men serve abroad and loyal arms support me, war never sleeps—I sit awake until dawn.

sentences.zh: 以維城之固，宜兼親賢，故使汝等未及師保之訓，皆弱年受任。

translations.literal: With the firmness of the cords that bind the city wall, one should combine kin and worthies; therefore I have made you, before the tutors' instruction, all receive office in weak years.
translations.idiomatic: A realm needs kin and worthies like cords around a wall, so I have given you office young, before tutors could finish your training.

sentences.zh: 常懼弗克，以貽咎悔。

translations.literal: I constantly fear not being able to succeed, thereby leaving blame and regret.
translations.idiomatic: I dread daily that I may fail you and leave you shame and regret.

sentences.zh: 古今之事不可以不知，苟近而可師，何必遠也。

translations.literal: Matters of past and present cannot be unknown; if what is near can serve as teacher, why must it be far?
translations.idiomatic: Past and present are a mirror: what lies close at hand can teach—why search far off?

sentences.zh: 覽諸葛亮訓勵，應璩奏諫，尋其終始，周孔之教盡在中矣。

translations.literal: Read Zhuge Liang's admonitions and Ying Qu's memorial remonstrances; seek their beginning and end—the teaching of Zhou and Kong lies complete therein.
translations.idiomatic: Read Zhuge Liang's warnings and Ying Qu's frank memorials from start to finish; the way of the sages is all there.

sentences.zh: 為國足以致安，立身足以成名，質略易通，寓目則了，雖言發往人，道師於此。

translations.literal: For ordering a state it is enough to bring peace; for establishing the person it is enough to make a name; the substance is plain and easy to penetrate—one glance and it is clear; although the words issue from men of old, the way takes them as teacher here.
translations.idiomatic: They teach how to settle a state and build a man in plain words—clear at a glance—yet though ancient men spoke them, they are masters for us today.

sentences.zh: 且經史道德如采菽中原，勤之者則功多，汝等可不勉哉！

translations.literal: Moreover the classics, histories, and virtue are like picking beans in the central plain—those who labor at them have much merit—how can you not exert yourselves!"
translations.idiomatic: The classics and histories are like gleaning beans in the heartland—the more you toil, the more you gain—so strive!"

sentences.zh: 」玄盛乃修敦煌舊塞東西二圍，以防北虜之患，築敦煌舊塞西南二圍，以威南虜。

translations.literal: Xuansheng thereupon repaired Dunhuang's old barrier, east and west two enclosures, to guard against northern Lu trouble, and built Dunhuang's old barrier southwest two enclosures, to awe the southern Lu.
translations.idiomatic: He then rebuilt the old Dunhuang wall, twin ramparts east and west against the northern tribes, and twin works southwest to overawe the south.

sentences.zh: 玄盛以緯世之量，當呂氏之末，為群雄所奉，遂啟霸圖，兵無血刃，坐定千里，謂張氏之業指期而成，河西十郡歲月而一。

translations.literal: Xuansheng, with the capacity to order the age, at the Lu clan's end, was elevated by the host of heroes; thereupon he opened hegemonic plans; arms without blood on blades, he sat and settled a thousand li; he said the Zhang house's enterprise could be completed on schedule, the ten commanderies of Hexi unified in months.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xuansheng, a man fit to rule the times, was raised by the heroes at the fall of the Lu; he opened a hegemon's design and, almost without bloodshed, stilled a thousand li. He thought the Zhangs' work could be finished on a timetable and the ten Hexi commanderies gathered in months.

sentences.zh: 既而禿髮傉檀入據姑臧，且渠蒙遜基宇稍廣，於是慨然著《述志賦》焉，其辭曰：

translations.literal: Soon Tufa Rutan entered and occupied Guzang, and Juqu Mengxun's foundation and roof gradually broadened; thereupon he sighed and composed the "Rhapsody on Stating My Purpose"; its words say:
translations.idiomatic: Then Tufa Rutan seized Guzang and Juqu Mengxun's power swelled; he sighed and wrote his "Rhapsody on Stating My Purpose," which runs:

sentences.zh: 涉至虛以誕駕，乘有輿於本無，稟玄元而陶衍，承景靈之冥符。

translations.literal: I cross utmost void to yoke the carriage, ride the existent carriage on root non-being, receive dark origin and mold its spread, inherit bright spirits' silent tally.
translations.idiomatic: Through the void I rein my chariot, ride form on the formless, draw dark source into the world, and take Heaven's silent tally.

sentences.zh: 廕朝雲之庵藹，仰朗日之照煦。

translations.literal: Shaded by morning cloud's thick haze, I look up to the bright sun's warming shine.
translations.idiomatic: Veiled in morning mist, I lift my face to the sun's warmth.

sentences.zh: 既敷既載，以育以成。

translations.literal: Already spread, already loaded—thereby to nurture, thereby to complete.
translations.idiomatic: Once spread and filled, they breed and bring all to completion.

sentences.zh: 幼希顏子曲肱之榮，遊心上典，玩禮敦經。

translations.literal: In youth I hoped for Yan Hui's glory of bent elbow, roamed the mind on high canons, played with ritual and thickened the classics.
translations.idiomatic: In youth I envied Yan Hui's joy in a bent elbow, fed my mind on the classics, and steeped myself in ritual.

sentences.zh: 蔑玄冕於硃門，羨漆園之傲生；

translations.literal: I scorned the dark crown at vermilion gates, envied the proud life of Lacquer Garden;
translations.idiomatic: I scorned court caps at vermillion gates and envied Zhuangzi in his lacquer garden;

sentences.zh: 尚漁父于滄浪，善沮溺之耦耕，穢鵄鳶之籠哧，欽飛鳳於太清；

translations.literal: I honored the fisherman on the Canglang, praised the paired ploughing of Ju and Ni, reviled the kites' cage-cry, admired the phoenix soaring in highest clarity;
translations.idiomatic: I praised the Canglang fisherman and Ju and Ni at the plough, loathed the kite's cage-cry, loved the phoenix in clear sky;

sentences.zh: 杜世競於方寸，絕時譽之嘉聲。

translations.literal: I blocked worldly strife within a square inch, cut off timely praise's lovely sound.
translations.idiomatic: I shut out the world's scramble in a square inch and silenced the hunger for fame.

sentences.zh: 超霄吟於崇嶺。

translations.literal: I transcended night song on lofty peaks.
translations.idiomatic: I rose above night song on high peaks.

sentences.zh: 奇秀木之陵霜；

translations.literal: I marveled at the strange tree that braves frost;
translations.idiomatic: I marveled at the rare tree that defies frost;

sentences.zh: 挺修幹之青蔥，經歲寒而彌芳。

translations.literal: Straight tall stems, green and lush, passing year-cold yet more fragrant.
translations.idiomatic: Straight stems, green through winter, growing sweeter in the cold.

sentences.zh: 情遙遙以遠寄，想四老之暉光；

translations.literal: My mood floated far to lodge afar, thinking on the four elders' radiant light;
translations.idiomatic: My heart drifted far, drawn to the four white-haired recluses' gleam;

sentences.zh: 將戢繁榮于常衢，控雲轡而高驤；

translations.literal: I would gather riotous glory on the common road, yet rein cloud horses to gallop high;
translations.idiomatic: I would leave the common road's riot, yet rein cloud-steeds to gallop high;

sentences.zh: 攀瓊枝于玄圃，漱華泉之淥漿；

translations.literal: I would climb jade branches in the dark garden, rinse with flowery spring's green waters;
translations.idiomatic: Climb jade boughs in the mystic garden, rinse in flower-spring's green stream;

sentences.zh: 和吟鳳之逸響，應鳴鸞于南岡。

translations.literal: Harmonize with the phoenix's wandering tone, answer the calling luan on southern hills.
translations.idiomatic: Match the phoenix's wandering cry, answer the calling simurgh on southern hills.

sentences.zh: 時弗獲青彡，心往形留，眷駕陽林，宛首一丘；

translations.literal: Time did not grant leisure; the heart went but the form remained; I yearned toward sunny groves, bent my head to one hill;
translations.idiomatic: Time never granted ease: mind flew but the body stayed; I longed for sunlit woods yet bowed to a single hill;

sentences.zh: 沖風沐雨，載沈載浮。

translations.literal: I met rushing wind and drenching rain, now sunk, now floating.
translations.idiomatic: Wind and rain struck; I sank and rose with the flood.

sentences.zh: 利害繽紛以交錯，歎感迴圈而相求。

translations.literal: Gain and loss tangled and crossed; sighs and feelings circled and sought each other.
translations.idiomatic: Gain and loss snarled together; grief and longing chased in circles.

sentences.zh: 乾扉奄寂以重閉，天地絕津而無舟；

translations.literal: Heaven's gate suddenly stilled and double-closed; heaven and earth cut the ford and had no boat;
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's gate slammed shut; heaven and earth broke the ford—no boat;

sentences.zh: 悼貞信之道薄，謝慚德於圜流。

translations.literal: I mourned that the way of steadfast trust grew thin; I apologized, ashamed of virtue, to the circling flow.
translations.idiomatic: I mourned how thin loyalty had grown and begged pardon of the turning stream for my failing virtue.

sentences.zh: 遂乃去玄覽，慶世賓，肇弱巾於東宮，並羽儀于英倫，踐宣德之秘庭，翼明後於紫宸。

translations.literal: Thereupon I left dark contemplation, became the age's guest, first tied a weak cap in the eastern palace, joined winged pageantry among splendid peers, trod the secret court of displaying virtue, aided the bright lord in the purple palace.
translations.idiomatic: So I left reclusion, entered the world, bound a youth's cap in the eastern palace, joined splendid peers, trod halls of virtue, and served the bright lord in the purple depths.

sentences.zh: 赫赫謙光，崇明奕奕，岌岌王居，詵詵百辟，君希虞夏，臣庶夔益。

translations.literal: Brilliant was modest light; high shone clarity; steep stood the royal residence; many were the hundred lords; the lord hoped to match Yu and Xia; ministers were many as Kui and Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Brilliant modesty shone; the throne rose steep; lords thronged the hall; the ruler sought Yu and Xia; ministers strove like Kui and Yi.

sentences.zh: 張王頹岩，梁後墜壑，淳風杪莽以永喪，搢紳淪胥而覆溺。

translations.literal: The Zhang kings fell from cliff; the Liang queen dropped into gorge; pure wind in distant wastes was lost forever; girdle-pendants sank together and overturned in drowning.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhang kings fell from the heights, the Liang line into the pit; pure wind died in the wilds; the gentry drowned together.

sentences.zh: 呂發釁於閨牆，厥構摧以傾顛；

translations.literal: The Lu raised quarrel within women's quarters; its frame was smashed and toppled;
translations.idiomatic: The Lu house bred strife in the inner chambers and saw its rafters crash;

sentences.zh: 疾風飄于高木，回湯沸於重泉；

translations.literal: Gale wind blew on high trees; whirling soup boiled in deep springs;
translations.idiomatic: Storm wind struck the treetops; boiling surge churned the deep springs;

sentences.zh: 飛塵翕以蔽日，大火炎其燎原；

translations.literal: Flying dust gathered to hide the sun; great fire blazed across the plain;
translations.idiomatic: Dust clouds hid the sun; wildfire raced the plain;

sentences.zh: 名都幽然影絕，千邑闃而無煙。

translations.literal: Famed capitals fell still, shadow gone; a thousand towns were empty without smoke.
translations.idiomatic: Great cities went dark; a thousand towns stood empty, without a cooking smoke.

sentences.zh: 斯乃百六之恆數，起滅相因而迭然。

translations.literal: This is indeed the hundred-six's constant number—rise and extinction follow each other in turn.
translations.idiomatic: So runs fate's hundred-six cycle—rise and ruin chasing each other.

sentences.zh: 於是人希逐鹿之圖，家有雄霸之想，暗王命而不尋，邀非分於無象。

translations.literal: Therefore men scarce for maps of chasing the deer, every house had thoughts of hegemony, dim to the king's command and not seeking it, inviting improper share from formless chance.
translations.idiomatic: Then every man craved the deer, every house dreamed of empire, forgot the king's mandate, and grasped at more than fate allows.

sentences.zh: 故覆車接路而繼軌，膏生靈於土壤。

translations.literal: Therefore overturned carts linked the road and followed ruts, smearing the living on soil and mud.
translations.idiomatic: Wrecked chariots lined the roads; the people were ground into mud.

sentences.zh: 哀餘類之忪懞，邈靡依而靡仰；

translations.literal: I pitied the rest of my kind, trembling, far with none to rely on, none to look up to;
translations.idiomatic: I pitied our remnant folk, trembling, with nowhere to lean;

sentences.zh: 求欲專而失逾遠，寄玄珠於罔象。

translations.literal: Seeking desire the more focused, the more the miss grew wide; I lodged the dark pearl in Formless.
translations.idiomatic: The tighter they clutched desire, the wider the miss; they sought the pearl in the imageless deep.

sentences.zh: 悠悠涼道。

translations.literal: Long, long—the road through Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Long, long ran the road through Liang—

sentences.zh: 鞠焉荒凶，杪杪餘躬，迢迢西邦，非相期之所會，諒冥契而來同。

translations.literal: It was utterly waste and woe; tiny, my remaining self; far, far, the western land—not a meeting place we planned, yet dark compact brought us the same.
translations.idiomatic: waste and woe; I, a speck of self, far in the west—not where I meant to be, yet fate drew us together.

sentences.zh: 跨弱水以建基，躡昆墟以為墉，總奔駟之駭轡，接摧轅於峻峰。

translations.literal: I crossed weak water to lay foundation, trod Kun's wastes for wall, gathered galloping teams' fearful reins, hitched broken shafts on steep peaks.
translations.idiomatic: We forded weak water for a base, took Kunlun's waste for walls, yoked frightened teams, and hitched broken axles to jagged peaks.

sentences.zh: 崇崖崨嶪，重險萬尋，玄邃窈窕，磐紆嶔岑，榛棘交橫，河廣水深，狐狸夾路，鴞鵄群吟，挺非我以為用，任至當如影響；

translations.literal: Lofty cliffs jagged, danger ten thousand fathoms deep; dark depth winding, rock twisted and peak steep; brambles crossed; rivers wide, waters deep; foxes lined the road, owls cried in flocks; I held what was not me to serve my use, trusting right fit like shadow and echo;
translations.idiomatic: Cliffs split the sky, gorges sank ten thousand feet; thorns choked the path, rivers ran wide; foxes and owls thronged the way; I used what was not mine, trusting rightness to answer like an echo;

sentences.zh: 執同心以禦物，懷自彼於握掌；

translations.literal: I grasped one heart to master things, held the other's self within my palm;
translations.idiomatic: With one heart I met events, held others as in my palm;

sentences.zh: 匪矯情而任荒，乃冥合而一往，華德是用來庭，野逸所以就鞅。

translations.literal: not feigning feeling yet trusting waste, then dark union in one forward stride; splendid virtue therefore came to court; wild recluses then took the bridle.
translations.idiomatic: not feigning yet trusting the void, I merged with fate in one stride; worth came to court, hermits took rein.

sentences.zh: 休矣時英，茂哉雋哲，庶罩網以遠籠，豈徒射鉤與斬袂！

translations.literal: Rest, o timely heroes; lush, o splendid wise—may you cast the far net, not merely shoot the hook or sever a sleeve!
translations.idiomatic: Rest, heroes of the hour; flourish, wise men—cast the wide net, not only the tales of hook and sleeve!

sentences.zh: 或脫梏而纓蕤，或後至而先列，采殊才于岩陸，拔翹彥於無際。

translations.literal: Some slipped stocks yet crowned with tassels; some came last yet ranked first; they gathered rare talent from rocky hills, plucked outstanding men from boundless waste.
translations.idiomatic: Some shook off chains for tasselled caps; some came late yet led the file; they drew genius from the crags and plucked sages from the wilds.

sentences.zh: 思留侯之神遇，振高浪以蕩穢；

translations.literal: I thought on Marquis Liu's divine meeting, raised high waves to wash away filth;
translations.idiomatic: I thought of the Marquis of Liu's fated meeting, raising waves to scour the mire;

sentences.zh: 想孔明於草廬，運玄籌之罔滯；

translations.literal: I pictured Kongming in the thatched hut, turning dark plans without obstruction;
translations.idiomatic: I pictured Kongming in his hut, turning dark strategies without halt;

sentences.zh: 洪操盤而慷慨，起三軍以激銳。

translations.literal: Great purpose coiled, generous and fervent, raising three armies to sharpen edge.
translations.idiomatic: Great purpose coiled, fervent, rousing three hosts to hone the blade.

sentences.zh: 詠群豪之高軌，嘉關張之飄傑，誓報曹而歸劉，何義勇之超出！

translations.literal: I chanted the heroes' high tracks, praised Guan and Zhang's swift valor, swore to repay Cao yet return to Liu—how their righteous courage leaped beyond!
translations.idiomatic: I sang the heroes' path, praised Guan and Zhang's lightning valor, their oath to quit Cao for Liu—courage past measure!

sentences.zh: 據斷橋而橫矛，亦雄姿之壯發。

translations.literal: They blocked the broken bridge and crossed spears—truly heroic mien in splendid outburst.
translations.idiomatic: They barred the broken bridge with leveled spears—heroic bearing in full flare.

sentences.zh: 輝輝南珍，英英周魯，挺奇荊吳，昭文烈武，建策烏林，龍驤江浦。

translations.literal: Bright southern treasures, splendid Zhou and Lu, strange talents rising in Jing and Wu, manifest in civil blaze and martial flame—plans laid at Wulin, dragon rising on the river shore.
translations.idiomatic: Bright southern pearls, Zhou and Lu's splendor, genius of Jing and Wu in civil flame and martial fire—strategy at Wulin, dragon banners on the Yangzi shore.

sentences.zh: 摧堂堂之勁陣，鬱風翔而雲舉，紹攀韓之遠蹤，侔徽猷于召武，非劉孫之鴻度，孰能臻茲大祜！

translations.literal: They shattered the mighty battle line, wind soaring, clouds lifting; they continued Han's far tracks, matched fine plans to Shao and Wu—without Liu and Sun's vast measure, who could reach such great blessing!
translations.idiomatic: They broke the mighty line, wind and cloud lifting; they traced Han's path, rivaled Shao and Wu in design—without Liu and Sun's vast scope, who could win such fortune!

sentences.zh: 信乾坤之相成，庶物希風而潤雨。

translations.literal: Truly heaven and earth complete each other; the myriad things hope for wind and are moistened by rain.
translations.idiomatic: Truly heaven and earth complete each other; creation waits on wind and rain.

sentences.zh: 崏益既蕩，三江已清，穆穆盛勳，濟濟隆平，禦群龍而奮策，彌萬載以飛榮，仰遺塵於絕代，企高山而景行。

translations.literal: Min and Yi already swept, three rivers already clear; solemn great merit, many in peace and rise; driving the flock of dragons with whip, filling ten thousand years with flying glory; I look up to dust-tracks of a cut-off age, stand on tiptoe toward high hills and bright conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Ba and Shu were stilled, the three rivers cleared; glorious merit, peace in hosts; driving dragons with the whip, glory for ten thousand years; I gaze at tracks of a lost age and crane toward peaks of bright example.

sentences.zh: 將建硃旗以啟路，驅長轂而迅征，靡商風以抗旆，拂招搖之華旌，資神兆於皇極，協五緯之所寧。

translations.literal: I will raise vermilion banners to open the road, drive long hub-ends in swift march, lean on west wind to lift the pennant, brush the Dipper's splendid flags, rely on divine omens at the pole, harmonize what the five cords secure.
translations.idiomatic: I will raise scarlet banners, race long axles on swift march, lean on autumn wind for the pennant, brush the Dipper's bright flags, trust omens at the pole, align the five planets' peace.

sentences.zh: 赳赳幹城，翼翼上粥，恣馘奔鯨，截彼丑類。

translations.literal: Stalwart shield-wall, winged ministers assisting the throne, freely cut fleeing whales, sever those ugly kinds.
translations.idiomatic: Stalwart shields, ministers like wings at the throne, hew the fleeing whale, cut off the vile breed.

sentences.zh: 且灑游塵于當陽，拯涼德於已墜。

translations.literal: Moreover sprinkle wandering dust at Dangyang, raise Liang virtue from its fall.
translations.idiomatic: Wash the dust at Dangyang, raise fallen Liang virtue from the dust.

sentences.zh: 間昌寓之驂乘，暨襄城而按轡。

translations.literal: I shall join Chang Yu's outriders, rein in at Xiangcheng and check the bit.
translations.idiomatic: I shall ride with Chang Yu's escort, halt at Xiangcheng and gather rein.

sentences.zh: 知去害之在茲，體牧童之所述，審機動之至微，思遺餐而忘寐，表略韻於紈素，托精誠于白日。

translations.literal: Knowing harm's removal lies herein, embodying the herd boy's saying, discerning how subtle the trigger is, thinking of leaving a meal and forgetting sleep, sketching brief rhyme on white silk, lodging earnest heart in the bright sun.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing here lies the cure, taking the herd boy's lesson, seeing how fine the trigger, forgetting food and sleep, tracing brief verse on silk, pledging my heart to the sun.

sentences.zh: 玄盛寢疾，顧命宋繇曰：「吾少離荼毒，百艱備嘗，於喪亂之際，遂為此方所推，才弱智淺，不能一同河右。

translations.literal: When Xuansheng lay gravely ill, he entrusted Song Yao with final commands, saying: "In youth I left bitter poison; a hundred hardships I fully tasted; amid loss and chaos I was then pushed by this quarter; talent slight, wisdom shallow—I could not unify the west of the river.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xuansheng, dying, told Song Yao, "I tasted bitterness young and every hardship in the ruin; this land raised me, though my talent was slight and I never united the Hexi.

sentences.zh: 今氣力惙然，當不復起矣。

translations.literal: Now my strength is utterly spent; I shall not rise again.
translations.idiomatic: My strength is spent; I will not rise again.

sentences.zh: 死者大理，吾不悲之，所恨志不申耳。

translations.literal: Death is the great pattern—I do not grieve it; what I resent is that my will was not fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: Death is nature's law—I do not mourn it; I only regret unfinished purpose.

sentences.zh: 居元首之位者，宜深誡危殆之機。

translations.literal: Those who occupy the chief's place ought deeply to warn themselves of the pivot of peril.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever sits first must heed the brink of ruin.

sentences.zh: 吾終之後，世子猶卿子也，善相輔導，述吾平生，勿令居人之上，專驕自任。

translations.literal: After my end, the heir is as a son to you—well assist and guide him, narrate my whole life, do not let him dwell above others, alone proud and trusting himself.
translations.idiomatic: After I am gone the heir is your son—guide him, tell him my life, never let him lord it over others in pride.

sentences.zh: 軍國之宜，委之於卿，無使籌略乖衷，失成敗之要。

translations.literal: Military and state matters—entrust them to you; do not let plans stray from the center or miss the pivot of success and defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Army and state are yours—do not let counsel wander from the mark or miss the hinge of victory.

sentences.zh: 」十三年，薨，時年六十七。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he died, aged sixty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of his reign he died at sixty-seven.

sentences.zh: 國人上諡曰武昭王，墓曰建世陵，廟號太祖。

translations.literal: The people of the state submitted posthumous title Prince Wuzhao, tomb called Jianshi Mound, temple name Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: His people gave him the posthumous title Prince Wuzhao, buried him at the Jianshi tumulus, and named his temple Taizu.

sentences.zh: 先是，河右不生楸、槐、柏、漆，張駿之世，取于秦隴而植之，終於皆死，而酒泉宮之西北隅有槐樹生焉，玄盛又著《槐樹賦》以寄情，蓋歎僻陋遐方，立功非所也。

translations.literal: Earlier, west of the river catalpa, locust, cypress, and lacquer did not grow; in Zhang Jun's generation they were taken from Qin and Long and planted, and in the end all died, yet at the northwest corner of the Jiuquan palace a locust tree grew; Xuansheng again composed the "Rhapsody on the Locust Tree" to lodge his mood—thereby sighing that in a remote corner merit was not the place for it.
translations.idiomatic: Catalpa, locust, cypress, and lacquer would not grow in Hexi until Zhang Jun imported them from Qin and Long—all died—yet a locust sprouted at Jiuquan's northwest corner. Li Xuansheng wrote his "Rhapsody on the Locust Tree" to voice how far he was from the center where merit counts.

sentences.zh: 亦命主簿梁中庸及劉彥明等並作文。

translations.literal: He also ordered recorder Liang Zhongyong and Liu Yanming and others together to compose texts.
translations.idiomatic: He also set Liang Zhongyong, Liu Yanming, and others to compose matching pieces.

sentences.zh: 感兵難繁興，時俗喧競，乃著《大酒容賦》以表恬豁之懷。

translations.literal: Moved that arms-trouble arose thickly and the age's custom was noisy strife, he composed the "Great Wine-Vessel Rhapsody" to display a calm and open heart.
translations.idiomatic: Troubled by endless war and a shrill age, he wrote the "Great Wine-Vessel Rhapsody" to show a calm, open mind.

sentences.zh: 與辛景、辛恭靖同志友善，景等歸晉，遇害江南，玄盛聞而吊之。

translations.literal: With Xin Jing and Xin Gongjing he shared the same purpose and was friendly; when Jing and the others returned to the Jin and met harm south of the river, Xuansheng heard and mourned them.
translations.idiomatic: He was close to Xin Jing and Xin Gongjing; when they went south to the Jin and were killed, he mourned them from afar.

sentences.zh: 玄盛前妻，同郡辛納女，貞順有婦儀，先卒，玄盛親為之誄。

translations.literal: Xuansheng's former wife was a daughter of Xin Na of the same commandery—chaste and compliant, with a wife's deportment; she died first; Xuansheng personally for her composed a dirge.
translations.idiomatic: His first wife, Xin Na's daughter from his commandery, was chaste and proper; she died before him, and he wrote her dirge himself.

sentences.zh: 自餘詩賦數十篇。

translations.literal: Besides, poems and rhapsodies several tens of pieces.
translations.idiomatic: He left dozens of other poems and rhapsodies.

sentences.zh: 世子譚早卒，第二子士業嗣。

translations.literal: The heir Tan died early; the second son Shiye succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His heir Tan died young; the second son Shiye succeeded.

sentences.zh: 涼後主

translations.literal: Last ruler of Liang
translations.idiomatic: Last ruler of Liang

sentences.zh: 涼後主諱歆，字士業。

translations.literal: The last ruler of Liang's taboo name was Xin, style name Shiye.
translations.idiomatic: The last ruler of Liang was Li Xin, courtesy Shiye.

sentences.zh: 玄盛薨時，府僚奉為大都督、大將軍、涼公、領涼州牧、護羌校尉，大赦境內，改年為嘉興。

translations.literal: When Xuansheng died, the staff elevated him as grand commander-in-chief, grand general, duke of Liang, concurrently shepherd of Liang province, colonel who protects the Qiang, greatly amnestied the territory, and changed the year to Jiaxing.
translations.idiomatic: At Li Xuansheng's death his officers raised Li Xin to grand commander, grand general, Duke of Liang, governor of Liang, and colonel of the Qiang, proclaimed a general amnesty, and adopted the Jiaxing era.

sentences.zh: 尊母尹氏為太后，以宋繇為武衛將軍、廣夏太守、軍諮祭酒、錄三府事，索仙為征虜將軍、張掖太守。

translations.literal: They honored his mother Lady Yin as empress dowager, appointed Song Yao as General Who Guards the Marches, prefect of Guangxia, libationer of military counsel, recorder of the three offices' affairs, and Suo Xian as General Who Punishes Captives and prefect of Zhangye.
translations.idiomatic: They honored Lady Yin as empress dowager, named Song Yao guard general, prefect of Guangxia, war counsel, and recorder of the three bureaus, and Suo Xian as general who punishes captives and prefect of Zhangye.

sentences.zh: 且渠蒙遜遣其張掖太守且渠廣宗祚降誘士業，士業遣武衛溫宜等赴之，親勒大軍為之後繼。

translations.literal: Juqu Mengxun sent his Zhangye prefect Juqu Guangzong with a feigned surrender to lure Shiye; Shiye sent guard general Wen Yi and others to go to him and personally led the great army as rear support.
translations.idiomatic: Juqu Mengxun sent Juqu Guangzong of Zhangye with a sham capitulation to bait Li Shiye, who dispatched Wen Yi and followed with the main host.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜率眾三萬，設伏於蓼泉。

translations.literal: Mengxun led a host of thirty thousand and laid an ambush at Liaoyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun took thirty thousand men and ambushed him at Liaoyuan.

sentences.zh: 士業聞，引兵還，為遜所逼。

translations.literal: When Shiye heard it, he led troops back and was pressed by Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shiye turned back on the news and was harried by Mengxun.

sentences.zh: 士業親貫甲先登，大敗之，追奔百餘里，俘斬七千餘級。

translations.literal: Shiye personally donned armor and first ascended, greatly defeated him, pursued the rout more than a hundred li, and captured or cut more than seven thousand grades.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shiye armored himself and led the charge, shattered the enemy, chased them a hundred li, and killed or took over seven thousand.

sentences.zh: 明年，蒙遜又伐士業，士業將出距之，左長史張體順固諫，乃止。

translations.literal: The next year Mengxun again campaigned against Shiye; Shiye was about to go out to resist him; left chief clerk Zhang Tishun firmly remonstrated, and he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Mengxun struck again; Li Shiye meant to meet him in the field, but Zhang Tishun remonstrated until he stayed his hand.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜大芟秋稼而還。

translations.literal: Mengxun greatly mowed the autumn grain and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun stripped the autumn fields and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 是歲，朝廷以士業為持節、都督七郡諸軍事、鎮西大將軍、護羌校尉、酒泉公。

translations.literal: That year the court appointed Shiye credential holder, area commander of military affairs for seven commanderies, grand general who garrisons the west, colonel who protects the Qiang, and duke of Jiuquan.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Jin named him baton-bearing commander of seven commanderies, grand general who guards the west, colonel of the Qiang, and duke of Jiuquan.

sentences.zh: 士業用刑頗嚴，又繕築不止，從事中郎張顯上疏諫曰：「入歲已來，陰陽失序，屢有賊風暴雨，犯傷和氣。

translations.literal: Shiye used punishments rather harshly and also did not cease repairing and building; retainer Zhang Xian submitted a memorial remonstrating: "Since the year began, yin and yang have lost their order; repeatedly there have been violent winds and driving rains, injuring the harmonious qi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xin's justice ran harsh and his building never stopped; Zhang Xian memorialized: "Since the new year yin and yang have slipped their course; gales and storms have battered the harmonious breath.

sentences.zh: 今區域三分，勢不久並，並兼之本，實在農戰，懷遠之略，事歸寬簡。

translations.literal: Now the realm is split in three; the situation will not long remain tripartite; the root of annexation truly lies in farming and war; the strategy of cherishing the distant returns to lenience and simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: The realm is in three parts and cannot stay so; union rests on plow and spear; winning the far shore means mercy and ease.

sentences.zh: 而更繁刑峻法，宮室是務，人力凋殘，百姓愁悴。

translations.literal: Yet you multiply harsh laws and steep statutes and make palace chambers the task; human strength withers; the common people are anxious and haggard.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you heap cruel laws and chase palace work while men fail and the people groan.

sentences.zh: 致災之咎，實此之由。

translations.literal: The blame for bringing disaster is truly from this.
translations.idiomatic: These omens spring from this very fault.

sentences.zh: 」主簿氾稱又上疏諫曰：

translations.literal: Recorder Fan Cheng again submitted a memorial remonstrating, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Recorder Fan Cheng added a memorial that began:

sentences.zh: 臣聞天之子愛人後，殷勤至矣。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that Heaven's son loves mankind afterward—earnest and utmost.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that Heaven's Son loves the people with tireless care.

sentences.zh: 故政之不修，則垂災譴以戒之。

translations.literal: Therefore when government is not cultivated, then it hangs calamity and reproof to warn.
translations.idiomatic: When rule falters, Heaven sends warnings.

sentences.zh: 改者雖危必昌，宋景是也；

translations.literal: Those who reform, though in peril, must flourish—Duke Jing of Song is the example;
translations.idiomatic: Change your ways and even peril turns to fortune—that was Duke Jing of Song;

sentences.zh: 其不改者，雖安必亡，虢公是也。

translations.literal: those who do not reform, though at peace, must perish—the duke of Guo is the example.
translations.idiomatic: refuse reform and even peace ends in ruin—that was the duke of Guo.

sentences.zh: 元年三月癸卯，敦煌謙德堂陷；

translations.literal: In the first year, third month, guimao, Dunhuang's Qiande Hall sank;
translations.idiomatic: In the first year, third month, day guimao, Dunhuang's Hall of Modest Virtue collapsed;

sentences.zh: 八月，效谷地烈；

translations.literal: eighth month, Xiaogu ground split;
translations.idiomatic: in the eighth month the soil of Xiaogu cracked;

sentences.zh: 二年元日，昏霧四塞；

translations.literal: second year new year's day, dusk fog blocked the four sides;
translations.idiomatic: on New Year's day of the second year fog sealed every quarter;

sentences.zh: 四月，日赤無光，二旬乃復；

translations.literal: fourth month, the sun was red without light, and after two ten-day weeks then recovered;
translations.idiomatic: in the fourth month the sun burned dull red for twenty days before clearing;

sentences.zh: 十一月，狐上南門；

translations.literal: eleventh month, a fox climbed the south gate;
translations.idiomatic: in the eleventh month a fox scaled the south gate;

sentences.zh: 今茲春夏地頗五震；

translations.literal: this year spring and summer the earth has quaked rather often in five places;
translations.idiomatic: this spring and summer the earth shook five times;

sentences.zh: 六月，隕星于建康。

translations.literal: sixth month, a shooting star fell at Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: in the sixth month a meteor fell on Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 臣雖學不稽古，敏謝仲舒，頗亦聞道于先師，且行年五十有九，請為殿下略言耳目之所聞見，不復能遠論書傳之事也。

translations.literal: Your subject, although learning does not investigate antiquity, keenness falls short of Zhongshu, yet also has heard the way from former teachers, and moreover in walking years is fifty-nine; I beg to speak for Your Highness in brief of what eye and ear have heard and seen—I can no longer discourse far on book and tradition matters.
translations.idiomatic: I am no scholar to match Dong Zhongshu, yet at fifty-nine I have heard teachers' lessons and will tell you only what I have seen—no distant book lore.

sentences.zh: 乃者咸安之初，西平地烈，狐入謙光殿前，俄而秦師奄至，都城不守。

translations.literal: In old days at the beginning of Xianan, Xiping ground split, a fox entered before the Modest Light Hall, and soon Qin troops arrived suddenly; the capital city did not hold.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xianan the earth split at Xiping, a fox entered the Modest Light Hall, and Qin armies soon took the capital.

sentences.zh: 梁熙既為涼州，藉秦氏兵亂，規有全涼之地，外有撫百姓，內多聚斂，建元十九年姑臧南門崩，隕石於閑豫堂，二十年而呂光東反，子敗於前，身戮於後。
