translations.literal: After Liang Xi became Liangzhou, riding Qin clan soldiers' turmoil, he planned to hold all Liang land—without he soothed the common people, within he piled up levies; in Jianyuan's nineteenth year Guzang's south gate collapsed, a meteorite fell at the Idle Ease Hall, and in the twentieth year Lu Guang rebelled east, his son defeated before, himself executed after.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Xi seized Liangzhou in Qin's chaos, taxed the people within while claiming to soothe them without—then Guzang's south gate fell, a stone struck the Idle Ease Hall, and in the twentieth year Lu Guang revolted eastward, his son ruined before him, himself slain after.

sentences.zh: 段業因群胡創亂，遂稱制此方，三年之中，地震五十餘所，既而先王龍興瓜州，蒙遜殺之張掖。

translations.literal: Duan Ye because the host of Hu created turmoil thereupon styled himself ruler of this quarter; within three years, earthquakes were more than fifty; soon afterward the former king rose like a dragon at Guazhou, and Mengxun killed him at Zhangye.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Ye rode tribal revolt to claim power; fifty quakes shook the land in three years; then your father rose at Guazhou until Mengxun slew him at Zhangye.

sentences.zh: 此皆目前之成事，亦殿下之所聞知。

translations.literal: These are all completed affairs before the eyes and also what Your Highness has heard and knows.
translations.idiomatic: These are facts before your eyes and well within your memory.

sentences.zh: 效谷，先王鴻漸之始，謙德，即尊之室，基陷地裂，大凶之征也。

translations.literal: Xiaogu was the place where the former king first rose like a goose; Qiande is the chamber where he took honored rank; foundation sank and earth split—an omen of great ill.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaogu was where your father first spread his wings; Qiande was the hall of his enthronement—their ruin and cracking are dire signs.

sentences.zh: 日者太陽之精，中國之象，赤而無光，中國將為胡夷之所陵滅。

translations.literal: The sun is the essence of great yang, the image of the central states; red yet without light—the central states will be overrun and extinguished by Hu and Yi.
translations.idiomatic: The sun stands for the throne; dull crimson means the heartland will fall to steppe peoples.

sentences.zh: 諺曰：「野獸入家，主人將去。

translations.literal: The proverb says: "When wild beasts enter the house, the master will depart.
translations.idiomatic: The proverb runs, "Beasts in the hall mean the master must leave.

sentences.zh: 」今狐上南門，亦災之大也。

translations.literal: Now the fox climbed the south gate—again a great calamity."
translations.idiomatic: A fox on the south gate is calamity indeed."

sentences.zh: 又狐者胡也，天意若曰將有胡人居於此城，南面而居者也。

translations.literal: Moreover the fox is the Hu; Heaven's intent seems to say that Hu men will dwell in this city, facing south to live.
translations.idiomatic: Fox sounds like "Hu": Heaven warns that Hu will hold this city and face south as lords.

sentences.zh: 昔春秋之世，星隕于宋，襄公卒為楚所擒。

translations.literal: In old days in the Spring and Autumn era a star fell in Song, and Duke Xiang in the end was captured by Chu.
translations.idiomatic: When a star fell on Song in the Spring and Autumn era, Duke Xiang ended in Chu's hands.

sentences.zh: 地者至陰，胡夷之象，當靜而動，反亂天常，天意若曰胡夷將震動中國，中國若不修德，將有宋襄之禍。

translations.literal: Earth is utmost yin, the image of Hu and Yi; it ought to be still yet moves, contrary to Heaven's constant; Heaven's intent seems to say the Hu and Yi will shake the central states; if the central states do not cultivate virtue, there will be the disaster of Duke Xiang of Song.
translations.idiomatic: Earth is yin—the barbarians' image; when it stirs, Heaven warns that they will shake China unless China returns to virtue, as at Song Xiang's disaster.

sentences.zh: 臣蒙先朝布衣之眷，輒自同子弟之親，是以不避忤上之誅，昧死而進愚款。

translations.literal: Your subject has received the former court's favor as a plain-clothed man and rashly identifies himself with the closeness of sons and younger brothers; therefore I do not avoid execution for offending superiors and, in death's face, advance foolish sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: I ate the old court's bread like a son of the house, so I risk your anger to speak plain truth.

sentences.zh: 願殿下親仁善鄰，養威觀釁，罷宮室之務，止遊畋之娛。

translations.literal: I hope Your Highness will be kind to the good and kind to neighbors, nurture awe and watch for openings, cease palace tasks, and stop hunting and roaming pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: Befriend the worthy and your neighbors, husband your strength and watch for your chance, end palace works, and give up the chase.

sentences.zh: 後宮嬪妃、諸夷子女，躬受分田，身勸蠶績，以清儉素德為榮，息茲奢靡之費，百姓租稅，專擬軍國。

translations.literal: Palace rear concubines and various Yi children's daughters—personally receive allotted fields, personally urge silkworm work, take clear frugality and plain virtue as glory, rest this extravagant waste, and let the common people's rent and tax be earmarked solely for army and state.
translations.idiomatic: Put consorts and tribal girls to field and loom, honor plain living, stop waste, and pour every grain of rent into defense.

sentences.zh: 虛衿下士，廣招英雋，修秦氏之術，以強國富俗。

translations.literal: Empty the breast to humble yourself before scholars, broadly summon outstanding men, cultivate the Qin house's methods, thereby to strengthen the state and enrich custom.
translations.idiomatic: Humble yourself to talent, call in heroes, use Qin's methods of state, and enrich people and law.

sentences.zh: 待國有數年之積，庭盈文武之士，然後命韓白為前驅，納子房之妙算，一鼓而姑臧可平，長驅可以飲馬涇渭，方江面而爭天下，豈蒙遜之足憂！

translations.literal: Wait until the state has several years' store and the court overflows with civil and martial gentlemen, then command Han and Bai as vanguard, take in Zifang's subtle calculations—with one drum Guzang can be pacified, long drive can water horses at Jing and Wei, square the Yangzi face to contend for the realm—how could Mengxun be worth worry!
translations.idiomatic: When the bins are full and the hall bristles with talent, send your Han Xin and Bai Qi ahead with Zhang Liang's plots—one stroke takes Guzang, then you may water horses on the Jing and Wei and face the great river to win the realm. Mengxun would be nothing.

sentences.zh: 不然，臣恐宗廟之危必不出紀。

translations.literal: If not, your subject fears the ancestral temple's peril will not extend beyond a twelve-year cycle."
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise I fear the altars will fall within a twelve-year span."

sentences.zh: 士業並不納。

translations.literal: Shiye accepted none of it.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shiye ignored every word.

sentences.zh: 士業立四年而宋受禪，士業將謀東伐，張體順切諫，乃止。

translations.literal: In the fourth year after Shiye's establishment the Song received the abdication; Shiye was about to plan an eastern campaign; Zhang Tishun remonstrated sharply, and he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Four years into his reign the Liu Song took the mandate; Li Shiye meant to march east until Zhang Tishun talked him down.

sentences.zh: 士業聞蒙遜南伐禿髮傉檀，命中外戒嚴，將攻張掖，尹氏固諫，不聽，宋繇又固諫，士業並不從。

translations.literal: When Shiye heard that Mengxun south campaigned against Tufa Rutan, he ordered inner and outer alert, was about to attack Zhangye; Lady Yin firmly remonstrated; he did not listen; Song Yao again firmly remonstrated; Shiye accepted neither.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that Mengxun had gone south against Tufa Rutan, he mobilized for Zhangye; his mother Lady Yin and Song Yao begged him to stay his hand, but he refused both.

sentences.zh: 繇退而歎曰：「大事去矣，吾見師之出，不見師之還也！

translations.literal: Yao withdrew and sighed, saying: "The great matter is gone; I see the army go out but do not see the army return!"
translations.idiomatic: Song Yao withdrew, sighing, "The cause is lost—I see our host march out but not march home!"

sentences.zh: 」士業遂率步騎三萬東伐，鎰於都瀆澗。

translations.literal: Shiye thereupon led thirty thousand foot and horse east to campaign and encamped at the Dudu defile.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shiye then took thirty thousand foot and horse east and camped at the Dudu defile.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜自浩亹來，距戰於懷城，為蒙遜所敗。

translations.literal: Mengxun came from Haogan, met him in battle at Huai city, and Shiye was defeated by Mengxun.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun marched from Haogan to Huai and shattered Li Shiye there.

sentences.zh: 左右勸士業還酒泉，士業曰：「吾違太后明誨，遠取敗辱，不殺此胡，復何面目以見母也！

translations.literal: Those at his side urged Shiye to return to Jiuquan; Shiye said: "I disobeyed the empress dowager's clear instruction and far sought defeat and shame—unless I kill this Hu, with what face shall I again see my mother!"
translations.idiomatic: His staff begged him to run for Jiuquan; he cried, "I spurned my mother's counsel and marched to shame—if I do not kill this Hu, how can I face her?"

sentences.zh: 」勒眾復戰，敗於蓼泉，為蒙遜所害。

translations.literal: He compelled the host to fight again, was defeated at Liaoyuan, and met harm at Mengxun's hands.
translations.idiomatic: He forced another battle, lost at Liaoyuan, and died at Mengxun's hands.

sentences.zh: 士業諸弟酒泉太守翻、新城太守預、領羽林右監密、左將軍眺、右將軍亮等西奔敦煌，蒙遜遂入於酒泉。

translations.literal: Shiye's various younger brothers—Jiuquan prefect Fan, Xincheng prefect Yu, concurrently right guard of the feathered forest Mi, left general Tiao, right general Liang and others—fled west to Dunhuang, and Mengxun thereupon entered Jiuquan.
translations.idiomatic: His brothers Fan, Yu, Mi, Tiao, Liang, and the rest bolted west to Dunhuang while Mengxun walked into Jiuquan.

sentences.zh: 士業之未敗也，有大蛇從南門而入，至於恭德殿前；

translations.literal: Before Shiye's defeat, a great snake entered from the south gate as far as the front of the Reverent Virtue Hall;
translations.idiomatic: Before his fall a great serpent slid in the south gate to the Reverent Virtue Hall;

sentences.zh: 有雙雉飛出宮內；

translations.literal: a pair of pheasants flew out from within the palace;
translations.idiomatic: a pair of pheasants burst from the palace;

sentences.zh: 通街大樹上有烏鵲爭巢，鵲為烏所殺。

translations.literal: on a great tree in the open street crows and magpies fought for a nest, and the magpie was killed by the crow.
translations.idiomatic: on a main-street tree crows tore a magpie from its nest and killed it.

sentences.zh: 又有敦煌父老令狐熾夢白頭公衣帢而謂熾曰：「南風動，吹長木，胡桐椎，不中轂。

translations.literal: Moreover there was a Dunhuang elder, Linghu Chi, who dreamed a white-haired old man in headcloth said to Chi: "South wind rises, blows the long tree; the paulownia mallet does not fit the hub.
translations.idiomatic: A Dunhuang elder, Linghu Chi, dreamed a white-haired man in a kerchief say, "South wind rises, long timber bends; the paulownia peg will not fit the hub.

sentences.zh: 」言訖忽然不見。

translations.literal: When the words ended, suddenly he was not seen.
translations.idiomatic: He vanished before the words faded.

sentences.zh: 士業小字桐椎，至是而亡。

translations.literal: Shiye's childhood name was Tongchui; at this point he perished.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shiye's pet name was "Wooden Peg"—the riddle named his end.

sentences.zh: 翻及弟敦煌太守恂與諸子等棄敦煌，奔於北山，蒙遜以索嗣子遠緒行敦煌太守。

translations.literal: Fan and his younger brother Dunhuang prefect Xun, with various sons and others, abandoned Dunhuang and fled to the northern hills; Mengxun appointed Suo Si's son Yuanxu acting Dunhuang prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fan and his brother Li Xun fled the city for the northern hills; Mengxun put Suo Yuanxu in Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 元緒粗險好殺，大失人和。

translations.literal: Yuanxu was rough, perilous, and fond of killing, and greatly lost human harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Suo Yuanxu was brutal and bloody and lost every heart.

sentences.zh: 郡人宋承、張弘以恂在郡有惠政。

translations.literal: Commandery men Song Cheng and Zhang Hong because Xun in the commandery had benevolent government.
translations.idiomatic: Song Cheng and Zhang Hong knew Li Xun had ruled Dunhuang with kindness.

sentences.zh: 密信招恂。

translations.literal: They secretly sent a letter summoning Xun.
translations.idiomatic: They wrote secretly to call him back.

sentences.zh: 恂率數十騎入于敦煌，元緒東奔涼興，宋承等推恂為冠軍將軍、涼州刺史。

translations.literal: Xun led several tens of horsemen into Dunhuang; Yuanxu fled east to Liangxing; Song Cheng and others recommended Xun as General Who Crowns the Army and inspector of Liang province.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xun rode in with a few dozen horse; Yuanxu ran east to Liangxing; Song Cheng raised Li Xun to general and governor.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜遣世子德政率眾攻恂，恂閉門不戰，蒙遜自率眾二萬攻這，三面起隄，以水灌城。

translations.literal: Mengxun sent heir Dezheng to lead a host attacking Xun; Xun closed the gates and did not fight; Mengxun personally led a host of twenty thousand to attack Dunhuang, raised dikes on three sides, and used water to flood the city.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun sent his heir Dezheng; Li Xun shut the gates; Mengxun then brought twenty thousand men, ringed Dunhuang with dikes, and tried to drown it out.

sentences.zh: 恂遣壯士一千，連版為橋，潛欲決隄，蒙遜勒兵逆戰，屠其城。

translations.literal: Xun sent a thousand stalwarts, linked boards as a bridge, secretly wished to breach the dike; Mengxun led troops to meet them in battle and slaughtered the city.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xun sent a thousand men on a plank bridge to cut the dikes; Mengxun met them in battle and sacked the town.

sentences.zh: 士業子重耳，脫身奔于江左，仕于宋。

translations.literal: Shiye's son Chong'er escaped his body and fled to south of the Yangzi and served in the Song.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shiye's son Chong'er slipped away to the south and served the Liu Song.

sentences.zh: 後歸魏，為恆農太守。

translations.literal: Later he returned to Wei and became prefect of Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: He later went north to Wei and became prefect of Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜徙翻子寶等於姑臧，歲餘，北奔伊吾，後歸於魏，獨尹氏及諸女死于伊吾。

translations.literal: Mengxun moved Fan's son Bao and others to Guzang; after more than a year they fled north to Yiwu, afterward returned to Wei; only Lady Yin and the various daughters died at Yiwu.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun moved Li Fan's son Bao and kin to Guzang; a year later they fled to Yiwu, then to Wei, while Lady Yin and her daughters died in the desert.

sentences.zh: 玄盛以安帝隆安四年立，至宋少帝滅，據河右凡二十四年。

translations.literal: Xuansheng was established in Emperor An's Longan fourth year; down to the Song Emperor Shao's extinction, he held the west of the river altogether twenty-four years.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xuansheng rose in An's fourth Longan year; the house held Hexi twenty-four years until the Liu Song snuffed it out.

sentences.zh: 【史評】

translations.literal: Historian's appraisal
translations.idiomatic: Historian's commentary

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：王者受圖，咸資世德，猶混成之先大帝，若一氣之生兩儀。

translations.literal: The historian says: The king who receives the chart always relies on age-old virtue, like the great completion's prior great emperor, like one qi's birthing the two modes.
translations.idiomatic: The chronicler writes: A king who receives Heaven's chart rests on ages of piled virtue, as the cosmos bred the two poles from a single breath.

sentences.zh: 是以中陽勃興，資豢龍之構趾；

translations.literal: Therefore Zhongyang surged up, relying on the dragon-tamer's layered toe;
translations.idiomatic: So the Liu clan rose on piled merit like the dragon-tamer's tracks;

sentences.zh: 景亳垂統，本吞燕之開基。

translations.literal: Jing and Bo hung the line, rooted in swallow-swallowing's opening foundation.
translations.idiomatic: Shang took the mandate from swallowed Yan's ancient root.

sentences.zh: 涼武昭王英姿傑出，運陰陽而緯武，應變之道如神；

translations.literal: Prince Wuzhao of Liang's heroic bearing stood out; he turned yin and yang to weave martial order; the way of meeting change was like spirit;
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wuzhao of Liang stood heroically above his age, wove yin and yang into strategy, and read change like a spirit;

sentences.zh: 吞日月以經天，成物之功若歲。

translations.literal: he swallowed sun and moon to span heaven; the merit of completing things was like a year.
translations.idiomatic: he took sun and moon to thread the sky and ripened the realm like a harvest year.

sentences.zh: 故能懷茺弭暴，開國化家，宅五郡以稱籓，屈三分而奉順。

translations.literal: Therefore he could embrace waste and still violence, open a state and transform houses, settle five commanderies and declare vassalage, bend the tripartite division and offer obedience.
translations.idiomatic: He stilled chaos, opened a house, held five commanderies as vassal, and bowed to a realm split in three.

sentences.zh: 若乃《詩》褒秦仲，後嗣建削平之業；

translations.literal: As for how the Classic of Poetry praises Qin Zhong, and later heirs built the enterprise of leveling and pacifying;
translations.idiomatic: As the Odes praise Qin Zhong and his heirs built a pacifying reign;

sentences.zh: 頌美公劉，末孫興配天之祚。

translations.literal: it praises Duke Liu, and remote descendants raised the fortune matching Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: as they hymn Duke Liu whose distant line won Heaven-matching fortune;

sentences.zh: 或發跡於汧渭，或布化於邠岐，覆簣創元天之基，疏涓開環海之宅。

translations.literal: some rose from Qian and Wei, some spread transformation in Bin and Qi, overturned the basket to begin heaven's foundation, dredged streams to open the ring-sea's dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: some rose between Qian and Wei, some taught Bin and Qi—tilting the basket to lay heaven's base, cutting streams to open the encircling sea.

sentences.zh: 彼既有漸，此亦同符，是知景命攸歸，非一朝之可致，累功積慶，其所由來遠矣。

translations.literal: That already had gradualness; this too matches the tally—thereby one knows the bright mandate's return is not something one morning can bring; piled merit and accumulated blessing—their source comes from afar.
translations.idiomatic: They had their long growth; so did he—bright mandate is never won in a morning; piled merit travels a long road.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：武昭英睿，忠勇霸世。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Wuzhao was heroic and keen, loyal and brave, hegemon of the age.
translations.idiomatic: The eulogy reads: Wuzhao was keen and brave, a loyal hegemon of his day.

sentences.zh: 王室雖微，乃誠無替。

translations.literal: Although the royal house was slight, yet his sincerity did not falter.
translations.idiomatic: Though the Jin grew faint, his faith never wavered.

sentences.zh: 遺黎飲德，絕壤沾惠。

translations.literal: Surviving common people drank his virtue; cut-off soil touched his grace.
translations.idiomatic: Survivors drank his kindness; the farthest marches felt his grace.

sentences.zh: 積祉丕基，克昌來裔。

translations.literal: He piled blessing on the great foundation and could make the coming generations flourish.
translations.idiomatic: He heaped blessing on a great base and left his line to flourish.
